verdicts.explanation: The paper's abstract and Section 3.2.4 give this paper's own estimated ~5 mS/cm room-temperature conductivity for Li7NbO6 from FPMD Arrhenius extrapolation, so the value, material and computational origin are right, and the null secondary fields are correct.
The paper states that Feng et al. doped Li7NbO6 with tungsten to reach 0.28 mS/cm at room temperature, which is a literature value and matches the W dopant and literature_cited origin.

field_errors.evidence: its relatively high activation energy of 0.35 eV results in an estimated roomtemperature ionic conductivity of less than 0.1 mS/cm

verdicts.explanation: The paper gives only an upper bound ('less than 0.1 mS/cm'), not a value of 0.1, so recording 0.1 as the reported conductivity misrepresents the paper's result.

field_errors.evidence: the estimated ionic conductivity falls well below 0.1 mS/cm

verdicts.explanation: The paper only says the room-temperature conductivity falls well below 0.1 mS/cm, an unquantified bound, so storing 0.1 as the value is not what the paper reports.
The paper's Li5NaN2 section gives an estimated room-temperature conductivity of 4 mS/cm from its own FPMD Arrhenius fit with a 0.28 eV barrier, matching the record.

The paper says 'both materials' (undoped and Y-doped Li4Mo3O8) have the estimated 0.2 mS/cm room-temperature conductivity, so attributing the value to the undoped form alone is not supported by the text.
The paper states 'we estimate the ionic conductivity at room temperature to be 37 mS/cm' for Li4CO4 from this work's activation energy, so the value, material and computational origin are right.
The Fig. 8 caption attributes 2.16 mS/cm at 300 K for Li3Y(PS4)2 to ref 160 (Zhu, Chu and Ong), so the literature_cited origin and 300 K (26.85 °C) temperature are correct.
The Fig. 8 caption gives 0.22 mS/cm at 500 K for Li2CsI3 with ref 118 (Kahle et al.), matching the literature_cited origin and temperature.
The sentence attributes 28 mS/cm at 500 K to tetragonal-LGPO from Materzanini et al. (ref 84), so the value, temperature and literature_cited origin are right.
The same sentence attributes 6 mS/cm at 600 K to orthorhombic-LGPO from ref 84, matching the record's value, temperature and origin.
The paper states cubic-LLZO exhibits 20 mS/cm, a literature value, and gives no temperature for it, so the null temperature and empty dopants are consistent with the text.
